instrucciones:
Recibes registros de una base de reglas de producción audiovisual con IA. Cada registro trae su texto
literal completo, el documento y la ruta de encabezados donde está, y a veces un contexto (encabezado de tabla o de
bloque). El encabezado dice el alcance: modelo, régimen, etapa, caso. Para CADA registro devuelve:
- "enunciado": la regla en español, UNA frase: qué exige, prohíbe, limita o especifica. Si es un ejemplo o una
  explicación sin norma, empieza con "Ejemplo:" o "Explicación:".
- "alcance": a qué aplica exactamente según texto y encabezado (modelo y versión, caso, etapa, régimen) o "general".
- "temas": de 1 a 3 claves de la lista, las que mejor describen de qué trata.
Lista de temas (clave: descripción):

ubicaciones.encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 3. Text in image looks bad

registros.texto:
**Symptoms:** text is misspelled, kerning is off, font is wrong, multiple text elements compete.

**Causes:**
- Text was put in the image prompt instead of being composited
- Wrong generator chosen (using Midjourney for text-heavy work)
- Multiple text elements in one prompt

ubicaciones.encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 3. Text in image looks bad

registros.texto:
**Prompt-level fixes:**
- The right answer is almost always: **don't put text in the prompt**. Composite separately from `text-overlays.json`.
- If text must be in-image (poster work), use Ideogram v3 with explicit override flag
- Limit to one text element per prompt
- Use simple fonts (sans-serif, clean serif), cursive and decorative fonts fail even on Ideogram

ubicaciones.encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 3. Text in image looks bad

registros.texto: **Accept editorially when:** the deliverable genuinely requires baked-in text and Ideogram's output is close enough to retouch.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 4. Lighting direction inconsistency

registros.texto:
**Symptoms:** shot 3 has light from window-left, shot 4 has light from window-right, they cut together as a continuity error.

**Causes:**
- Lighting language paraphrased rather than verbatim from series_lock
- Reverse-angle shots not flagged in rationale
- Generator interpreting lighting ambiguously

ubicaciones.encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 4. Lighting direction inconsistency

registros.texto:
**Prompt-level fixes:**
- Verify lighting string is verbatim across prompts
- Be explicit about direction: "from camera-left" not "from one side"
- For reverse-angle shots, flag in rationale and update lighting language for that shot only
- For Flux and GPT Image, add the photographic spec ("key light camera-left at 45 degrees")

ubicaciones.encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 4. Lighting direction inconsistency

registros.texto: **Accept editorially when:** lighting drift is subtle enough that color grading will fix it.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 5. Composition doesn't reserve space for text overlay

registros.texto:
**Symptoms:** the storyboard says text goes in the right third, but the generated image has the subject filling the right third.

**Causes:**
- Shot subject didn't include negative-space note
- Generator interpreting "centered subject" by default

ubicaciones.encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 5. Composition doesn't reserve space for text overlay

registros.texto:
**Prompt-level fixes:**
- Add explicit composition note: "subject framed in left third, right two-thirds open for text overlay"
- For GPT Image (best at spatial reasoning), use percentage references: "subject at left 30% of frame"
- Re-roll with explicit composition prompt, this often fixes on second try

ubicaciones.encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 5. Composition doesn't reserve space for text overlay

registros.texto: **Accept editorially when:** image is otherwise great. Reposition text overlay to fit the actual composition.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 6. Series feels "different" even with locks applied

registros.texto:
**Symptoms:** all locks are in place, prompts look right, but the storyboard feels disjointed when viewed end-to-end.

**Causes:**
- Color grade language drifting between shots (one says "warm filmic", another says "cinematic")
- Aspect ratio drift (some 9:16 generations are taller than others)
- Mood adjectives shifting ("calm" in shot 1 vs "energetic" in shot 5 even though brief was uniform)

ubicaciones.encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 6. Series feels "different" even with locks applied

registros.texto:
**Prompt-level fixes:**
- Audit every prompt against series_lock and brand-lock, verbatim check
- Verify aspect ratio is identical across all prompts
- Lock the brand mood adjectives, same set in every prompt

ubicaciones.encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 6. Series feels "different" even with locks applied

registros.texto: **Accept editorially when:** the disjoint feel is below the noise floor for the medium (e.g. fast-cut social where each shot is on screen <2s).

ubicaciones.encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 7, "Looks fine but doesn't match the brief"

registros.texto:
**Symptoms:** image is technically good but doesn't capture what the brief was actually about.

**Causes:**
- The shot subject in `shots.json` was vague
- The brief context wasn't surfaced into the prompt
- The generator is producing competent generic output rather than specific intent

ubicaciones.encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 7, "Looks fine but doesn't match the brief"

registros.texto:
**Prompt-level fixes:**
- Tighten the shot's subject field, what specifically is the audience meant to feel or notice
- Include a one-phrase intent at the end ("the moment of recognition", "the calm before the decision")
- For complex scenes, add a "what this shot conveys" line

ubicaciones.encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 7, "Looks fine but doesn't match the brief"

registros.texto: **Accept editorially when:** generation is close enough that retouching gets there. Don't burn API credits chasing perfect on-prompt.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Failure Modes › When to stop iterating prompts

registros.texto:
Three signs:

1. You've re-rolled the same shot 5+ times with no improvement → the prompt is fine; the model can't render this concept; pick a different shot or different generator
2. You're tweaking single words and hoping → you've hit prompt-level diminishing returns; move to image-to-image refinement (Nano Banana) or post-production
3. The image is 80% right and the gap is editorial → ship to post and let the editor finish

ubicaciones.encabezado: Failure Modes › When to stop iterating prompts

registros.texto: Generation is one stage in a pipeline. Don't try to make it the whole pipeline.

Every image prompt this skill produces is composed from five layers. Four are inputs, one is applied at compose-time. Understanding the layers is the difference between bulletproof prompts and lottery tickets.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 1. Brand Lock

registros.texto:
**What:** the locked brand parameters for the entire project.
**Source:** `brand-lock.snapshot.md` referenced in `shots.json`.
**Constant across:** every storyboard, every shot.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 1. Brand Lock

registros.texto:
Contains:

- Palette (hex values)
- Typography (font names, weights)
- Mood descriptors (3–5 adjectives that describe the brand's emotional posture)
- "Never" list (things this brand never does, e.g. "no stock photo aesthetic", "no AI uncanny", "no over-saturated", "no shouting copy")
- Aspect ratios used
- Color grade direction

ubicaciones.encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 1. Brand Lock

registros.texto: This layer answers: **what does the brand always look and feel like?**

ubicaciones.encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 2. Series Lock

registros.texto:
**What:** the locked anchors for this specific storyboard.
**Source:** `shots.json` → `series_lock`.
**Constant across:** every shot in this one storyboard.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 2. Series Lock

registros.texto:
Contains:

- Character anchor (who's in frame, described identically every shot)
- Environment description (where the action takes place, identical every shot)
- Lighting setup (direction, source, color temperature, identical every shot)
- Color grade (filmic look, identical every shot)

ubicaciones.encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 2. Series Lock

registros.texto: This layer answers: **what stays the same across this storyboard?**

ubicaciones.encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 2. Series Lock

registros.texto: The series_lock is what makes shot 1 and shot 7 feel like the same piece. Without it, every generated frame looks like a different production.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 3. Shot Spec

registros.texto:
**What:** the per-shot variables.
**Source:** `shots.json` → `shots[i]`.
**Variable across:** every shot.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 3. Shot Spec

registros.texto:
Contains:

- Framing (ECU, CU, MS, etc.)
- Angle (eye-level, high, low, etc.)
- Motion (static, push, pull, etc.)
- Subject (what's happening in this specific shot)
- Depth of field
- Rationale (audit trail, why this shot, this beat, this moment)

ubicaciones.encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 3. Shot Spec

registros.texto: This layer answers: **what's different about this specific shot?**

ubicaciones.encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 4. Text Layer

registros.texto:
**What:** on-screen text composited after generation.
**Source:** `text-overlays.json`.
**Never appears in image prompts** (except Ideogram Mode 2 with explicit override).

ubicaciones.encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 4. Text Layer

registros.texto:
Why text is a separate layer:

1. **Editability.** Composited text can be revised without re-generating images.
2. **Quality.** Even Ideogram and GPT Image (the best at text) produce typography that lags professional design tools.
3. **Animation.** Animated text needs After Effects / Remotion / CapCut. Static rendered text is dead-on-arrival for motion content.
4. **Brand control.** Composited text uses exact brand fonts and exact brand colors. Generated text approximates.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 5. Generator Adapter

registros.texto:
**What:** model-specific syntax wrapper.
**Source:** the relevant `adapters/{generator}.md` file.
**Variable across:** every target generator.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 5. Generator Adapter

registros.texto: This is the only layer the skill *applies* (vs. reads). Layers 1–4 are inputs; Layer 5 is the renderer that turns inputs into a generator-specific string.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 5. Generator Adapter

registros.texto:
The adapter handles:

- Word order (Midjourney leads with subject; motion adapters like Kling lead with camera motion)
- Length conventions (Seedream short, GPT Image long)
- Parameter syntax (`--ar 9:16` vs `aspect_ratio: "9:16"`)
- Idiosyncratic strengths (Ideogram for text, Flux for photoreal, etc.)

ubicaciones.encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › How layers compose

registros.texto:
For a single shot's prompt:

```
Layer 1 (brand) ───┐
                   │
Layer 2 (series) ──┼──> Layer 5 (adapter) ──> {generator-specific prompt}
                   │
Layer 3 (shot) ────┘

Layer 4 (text) ────> separate compositing pipeline
```

ubicaciones.encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › How layers compose

registros.texto: The adapter pulls from Layers 1–3 and produces a string. Layer 4 lives parallel and never enters the prompt.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Why this matters operationally

registros.texto: **Change the brand color** → edit brand-lock.md. Every prompt across every storyboard updates. No find-and-replace across files.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Why this matters operationally

registros.texto: **Change the character** → edit series_lock in shots.json. Every shot in this storyboard updates. Other storyboards untouched.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Why this matters operationally

registros.texto: **Change one shot** → edit just that shot's spec. Other shots unaffected.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Why this matters operationally

registros.texto: **Change the generator** → swap adapters. Same shot data, different output file. Zero edits to brand-lock or series_lock.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Why this matters operationally

registros.texto: **Audit a render** → check brand-lock.snapshot.md to see what version the storyboard was built against.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Why this matters operationally

registros.texto: This is why guardrails-in-code beat guardrails-in-vibes. Each layer has one job. Changes are surgical. Outputs are reproducible.

Copia del linter del skill `aurora-prompt-linter` (v1.1, 2026-05-27) con el vocabulario
ampliado y las contradicciones con el resto del pipeline resueltas **a favor de la fuente**.
El original no se toca; vive en
`~/.claude/skills/synced/<id>/aurora-prompt-linter/scripts/` y sigue siendo la referencia
de la CLI. Esta copia conserva la misma interfaz (`--prompt --refs --case --platform --vocab
--overrides --sports-broadcast --json`), los mismos exit codes (`0` PASS, `1` FAIL, `2` uso)
y añade tres opciones: `--ref-role`, `--series-lock`, `--treatment`.

```
.claude/hooks/aurora/
├── prompt_linter.py      # copia parcheada; cabecera con changelog P1..P12 y fuente por parche
├── vocabularies.yaml     # vocabulario ampliado; se carga por defecto (o con --vocab)
├── README.md             # este archivo
└── tests/
    ├── run.sh            # 18 pruebas; exit 0 si todas pasan
    └── fixtures/         # prompts, refs, series_lock y mensaje de override
```
Requisitos: Python 3.11 y `pyyaml`. Nada más.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Aurora Prompt Linter — copia parcheada (v1.2-fupai) › Por qué existe esta copia

registros.texto:
El linter original es la única pieza del pipeline que convierte "no re-describir lo que está en
la referencia" en código. Eso es valioso y se conserva íntegro. El problema es que fue
calibrado para un flujo anterior (system v6.0, casos Aurora de ciclismo/fútbol) y, leído
junto a los skills que hoy gobiernan la producción (`video`, `image`, `visual-prompt-forge`,
`produccion-visual-sw30`, `ai-production-director`), **bloquea prompts que esos skills exigen**
y **deja pasar palabras que esos skills prohíben**. Las doce contradicciones están abajo, con
el parche que las resuelve y la fuente que lo sustenta. Ninguna decisión es de criterio del
agente: cada fila cita el archivo y la sección.

ubicaciones.encabezado: Aurora Prompt Linter — copia parcheada (v1.2-fupai) › Contradicción → parche → fuente
